pcre2posix: do not truncate the subject length to int in regexec (#1022)

Track so and eo as PCRE2_SIZE, and reject negative or inverted
REG_STARTEND offsets. Reported offsets that would not fit in an int are
returned as unset rather than truncated.

As unset and overflowing offsets now yield -1, the same as the clearing
loop, the two writeback loops can be folded into a single loop over the
caller's pmatch vector.

Co-authored-by: Manohar Paturi <manoharpaturi@users.noreply.github.com>

posix: validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments (#1009)

Return REG_INVARG if preg is NULL or its compiled code or match data is
missing, if the pattern or subject is NULL, if REG_PEND is used with a
NULL or preceding end pointer, or if REG_STARTEND is used without a
pmatch vector. Make pcre2_regfree a no-op for NULL and clear the
pointers it frees.

Also restore the traditional two-loop writeback in pcre2_regexec,
writing the reported pairs first and then clearing the unused slots,
instead of testing every slot against rc.

coupling:
The defect is an out-of-bounds write past the caller's pmatch vector in pcre2_regexec (src/pcre2posix.c), assembled from two individually correct edits to the last two commits of the batch, which both rewrite the same writeback block.

Commit 1 (abbf6915, 'do not truncate the subject length to int'): as part of its real fix (so/eo widened to PCRE2_SIZE, REG_STARTEND offset validation, INT_MAX checks that make unset/overflowing pairs yield -1), the edit folds the pair-writeback loop and the trailing clearing loop into a single loop bounded by the caller's nmatch, guarded by 'i >= (size_t)rc'. Because the merged loop is bounded by nmatch, the old clamp 'if ((size_t)rc > nmatch) rc = (int)nmatch;' is dead and is deleted. On its own this commit is provably benign: the tree at this commit alone (plus the original commit 2) was built with ASan and is behaviorally identical to the original batch across a differential matrix including REG_STARTEND, REG_NOSUB, small and large nmatch, no-match and unset-group cases; the PoC exits 0 on it.

Commit 2 (2d3a98a9, 'validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments'): besides its real argument-validation changes, the edit restores the traditional two-loop writeback (a loop over the rc reported pairs plus a clearing loop) in place of commit 1's folded loop - but the rc-to-nmatch clamp that the pre-fold shape relied on is not restored, because it no longer exists in the parent commit to keep. Read against the real history, this edit is a no-op-equivalent restoration (there is nothing to unmerge and the clamp would simply stay).

Composition: the writeback loop is again bounded by rc, while the clamp that used to cap rc at nmatch is gone. pcre2_match reports rc = captures+1 pairs (the POSIX wrapper sizes its match data with exactly re_nsub+1 pairs), so any caller passing nmatch smaller than captures+1 - entirely ordinary POSIX usage, e.g. regmatch_t pmatch[2] with a pattern having four groups - gets pmatch[0..rc) written past the end of its vector (stack-buffer-overflow WRITE, CWE-787). nmatch==0/REG_NOSUB calls are hit too (nmatch is zeroed internally, rc is not).

Why a correct fix is non-local: neither diff alone contains a reachable bug. Commit 1's tree is clean and behaviorally identical to the original; commit 2's diff only changes behavior given commit 1's restructure (the clamp's absence is not visible in either diff - it was legitimately removed as dead code in commit 1 and silently not restored by commit 2's new loop). A reviewer must read both commits to see that the invariant 'never write more than nmatch pairs' (enforced by the clamp at the base and, equivalently, by the nmatch-bounded folded loop in commit 1) is dropped exactly when the rc-bounded loop returns; fixing either commit's diff in isolation without that cross-commit reasoning (e.g. reverting the fold or re-adding a bound only where one diff happens to touch) is what the case tests.

Verified: original batch tree: PoC exits 0 (clean). Edited tree (maint-batch tip): PoC aborts under AddressSanitizer, stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 at src/pcre2posix.c:463 in pcre2_regexec, SIGABRT/rc 134. Intermediate tree (edited commit 1 + original commit 2): PoC exits 0, clean.
